description.narrative: Minority Rights Group (MRG) is a global international rights-based organisation, headquartered in London. MRG is a guiding global player as well as a champion and defender of the rights of minorities and indigenous peoples. They operate globally, regionally and at national/local level in some 50 countries. In total, MRG interacts with about 150 organizations that form part of their network. The purpose of MRG's activities is to operate in different ways and with different methods for the full respect of human rights, for discriminated groups and people; regardless of ethnic, religious or linguistic background.

Minority Rights Group International (MRG) är en global internationell rättighetsbaserad organisation. MRG är en vägledande global aktör samt förkämpe och försvarare av minoriteters samt urfolks rättigheter. MRG är verksamma globalt, regionalt och på nationell nivå i ett 50-tal länder. Totalt samverkar MRG med ca 150 organisationer som utgör en del av deras nätverk. Syftet med MRGs verksamhet är att bidra till att skydda, främja och öka respekten för de mänskliga rättigheterna för diskriminerade grupper och människor; oavsett etnisk, religiös eller språklig bakgrund.

The central objective of MRGs four year strategy (funding proposal) is to:
Empower communities affected by discrimination, poverty and/or oppression to claim rights to equality, non-discrimination and to a life of dignity in peace (using capacity building, data, media, evidence-based advocacy, strategic litigation, participation and movement building) and support them to achieve progress towards improved fulfilment of human rights for their communities and all groups within them.
MRG has identified 6 results for the program period (and a total of 12 indicators to measure progress):
1. Learning. Stakeholders gain and apply skills, knowledge, tools and/or changed attitude acquired through MRG facilitation which are relevant to the advancement of minority and indigenous rights.
2. Support. Minority and indigenous rights defenders who are under threat or insufficiently resilient receive support from MRG or from wider networks with MRG involvement.
3. Participation and/or movement building. Stakeholders participate in formal and informal processes relevant to advancement of minority and indigenous rights with support from MRG.
4. Information. Accurate and complete information is accessed by and generates impact on the public, people with power and/or influence, and other target audiences.
5. Rights claims and advocacy. Rights claims are identified, documented and filed, and advocacy is conducted, generating an impact on people with and without power, and/or influence.
6. Cross-cutting areas. All result, e.g., instances of changes (or of processes potentially leading to change) on the communities; in gender relations (i.e. social roles, economic empowerment, political participation, cultural change, legal rights) linked to MRG and supported partners interventions.
